nodes.name: ZIF-8 Encapsulation and Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Zn(NO3)2·6H2O (3 g) and Ga(acac)3 (200 mg) were dissolved in 40 ml methanol as solution A. 2-methylimidazole (6.5 g) was dissolved in 80 ml methanol as solution B. Then, two solutions were rapidly mixed under magnetic stirring for 24 h at room temperature. The precipitate was centrifuged, washed with methanol for three times and dried in an oven at 60 °C, followed by annealing at 900 °C for 2 h in a 5% H2/Ar atmosphere.

nodes.procedure: The N–C sample was prepared without the addition of Ga(acac)3 using the same procedure as GaSA/N-C: Zn(NO3)2·6H2O (3 g) dissolved in 40 ml methanol as solution A. 2-methylimidazole (6.5 g) was dissolved in 80 ml methanol as solution B. Then, two solutions were rapidly mixed under magnetic stirring for 24 h at room temperature. The precipitate was centrifuged, washed with methanol for three times and dried in an oven at 60 °C, followed by annealing at 900 °C for 2 h in a 5% H2/Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: Ru Cluster Anchoring
nodes.procedure: GaSA/N-C (50 mg) was mixed with Ru(acac)3 (18 mg) in a 100 mL beaker containing 40 ml ethanol. After evaporation, the dried powder was then subjected to high-temperature H2 reduction treatment in 5% H2/Ar at 400 °C for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM and TEM images show dodecahedral morphology of GaSA/N-C catalyst with porous structure and no metal nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images show the dodecahedral morphology of GaSA/N-C catalyst with porous structure, and no metal nanoparticles are formed during the pyrolysis process...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms dodecahedral morphology retained after Ru incorporation with ~1.8 nm bright Ru particles anchoring on GaSA/N-C support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the incorporation of Ru, the catalyst remains the dodecahedral morphology with apparent bright particles (~1.8 nm) anchoring on carbon support, indicating the successful incorporation of Ru clusters on the GaSA/N-C substrate...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms existence of Ga single atoms on N-C support and coexistence of Ru clusters (~1.8 nm) and Ga single atoms with Ga atoms partially distributed around Ru clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images of GaSA/N-C present the existence of Ga single atoms... Further HAADF-STEM image exhibits the coexistence of Ru clusters and Ga single atoms...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows Ru mainly distributes on cluster positions while Ga appears randomly on carbon support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping images display that Ru mainly distributes on the position of the clusters, while Ga appears randomly on the whole carbon support...

nodes.characterization_summary: BET test indicates Ru-GaSA/N-C possesses specific surface area of 1452.75 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) test of Ru–GaSA/N–C indicates that it possesses a large specific surface area of 1452.75 m² g⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Ru content of 7.98 wt% and Ga content of 0.94 wt% in Ru-GaSA/N-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) shows that the Ru and Ga contents of Ru–GaSA/N–C are 7.98 wt% and 0.94 wt%, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows only broad peak at 44° for Ru-GaSA/N-C indicating small Ru clusters, while Ru/N-C shows distinct peaks at 38°, 42°, 44° indicating larger particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the incorporation of Ru, only a broad peak at 44° can be observed for the Ru–GaSA/N–C catalyst, while distinct peaks at 38°, 42°, and 44° appear for the Ru/N-C sample...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ru 3p shows positive shift for Ru⁰ in Ru-GaSA/N-C vs Ru/N-C indicating lowered electron density; Ga 2p shows negative shift indicating electron transfer from Ru to Ga.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in the high-resolution Ru 3p spectra, the Ru⁰ peak of Ru–GaSA/N–C exhibits a positive shift relative to that of Ru/N-C... the peak of Ru–GaSA/N–C in the high-resolution Ga 2p spectra presents a negative shift...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows metallic Ru feature with positive edge shift; EXAFS shows Ru-Ru at 2.4 Å and Ru-N/C at 1.5 Å; Ga K-edge shows Ga³⁺ with Ga-N/C at 1.4 Å and Ga-Ru at 2.5 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra reveal that the absorption edges... approach that of Ru foil... EXAFS spectra... show a dominant peak at 2.4 Å... ascribed to the Ru–Ru bonding... a peak at around 2.5 Å exists... indicating the interaction between Ga atoms and Ru clusters...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ru/N-C catalyst has larger particle size of around 5.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By contrast, the Ru/N-C catalyst absence of Ga single atoms exhibits a larger particle size of around 5.5 nm, demonstrating the critical role of Ga single atoms in stabilizing Ru clusters...
